Definition: from G935; properly, royalty, i.e. (abstractly) rule, or (concretely) a realm (literally or figuratively):--kingdom, + reign.
BiblicalUsage: Basileia is the kingdom, the reign, the realm of a king. Jesus says the kingdom of heaven belongs to the poor in spirit, teaches us to pray for the kingdom to come, tells Nicodemus a man must be born again to see the kingdom of God, and John hears the seventh angel announce that the kingdoms of this world have become the kingdoms of our Lord and of His Christ.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the kingdom is not a place we build but a reign we enter, because Jesus says it belongs to the poor in spirit and comes to those who are born again. It is prayed for, it is preached, and one day it will be announced as finished, and I hold that every prayer for the kingdom to come is a prayer for the King to come.
